description: University of Louisville and North Carolina State University researchers publish Cardinal RF (CardRF), a collection of outdoor radio-frequency signals from UAV controllers, UAVs, Bluetooth devices and WiFi devices. The registered description distinguishes visual line-of-sight and beyond-line-of-sight acquisitions and reports more than 65 GB of data. AERPAW identifies MATLAB MAT files and describes individual signals with five million sampling points over 0.25 milliseconds. These are provider specifications, not independently checked sample timing. The provider identifies interference analysis and mitigation as uses, alongside RF fingerprinting and UAV identification, giving the data a concrete wireless communication performance role. IEEE DataPort hosts the 2022 release under CC BY 4.0. The current landing page could not be read, so download charges and registration requirements remain unknown. Exact acquisition dates, coordinates and complete field definitions are not established by the reviewed metadata. The experimental devices and acquisition conditions limit transfer to other wireless systems. The plotting script mentioned by AERPAW is supporting code and is not a separate resource here. No directly related active dataset was confirmed.
